title: A polyhedral study of the asymmetric traveling salesman problem with time windows
contribution: Gives an arc-variable-only model of the ATSP with time windows in which the time windows enter through infeasible path elimination constraints, lifts these into tournament, generalized-tournament, concatenation and V-lifted families, strengthens the (pi, sigma)-inequalities with time windows, and shows that even with a single active time window the polytope's dimension needs a Hamiltonian path computation (strongly NP-complete); the read file is ZIB Preprint SC 97-11 (February 1997) and contains no computation.
problem_entry: A ZIB industry project (stacker-crane moves in an automated storage system) and the success of polyhedral methods on the ATSP and the precedence-constrained ATSP; the standard model's big-M time linking is 'known to cause computational problems' and the alternative model adds |A| variables (pp. 3, 5).
key_idea: Keep only 0-1 arc variables and impose time windows by path no-goods x(P) <= |P| - 1, valid even with only the cheap deadline test of Lemma 2.1(i), then lift them through the transitive closure, sets of paths, cliques of clones, concatenations and V-lifting (pp. 5-6, 12-17).
assumptions: Open-path ATSP-TW on a complete digraph with integer costs, set-up and processing times, release dates and deadlines, waiting allowed; triangle inequality on theta in Lemma 2.1(ii), Section 3 and Theorems 4.9 and 4.12; polyhedral analysis only with one active time window; makespan or waiting-time objectives not expressible (pp. 2-3, 5-7, 15, 18).
proof_devices: Minimal equation system and dimension formula dim(P_TW) = |A| - (|Q| + m + mu) with one active time window: validity by contradiction, one violating point per equation for independence, affinely independent vertices from the closed-tour ATSP face plus an arborescence scan (Lemmas 3.4-3.5, Theorem 3.6), pp. 8-10
Strong NP-completeness of the dimension question by reduction from the bounded Hamiltonian path problem (Theorem 3.7), pp. 10-11
Tournament lifting of a path no-good from the degree constraints (Lemma 4.1), p. 12; set versions with easy sufficient infeasibility conditions (Theorems 4.3, 4.5, Lemma 4.7), pp. 13-14
V-lifting: two valid inequalities plus x_uh + x_hw + 2x_uw <= 2 weighted 1/2 and rounded, pp. 16-17
Facetness not proved; PORTA check that the inequalities are facets for most instances with n <= 5, p. 11
experiments: none in this paper; all computation is deferred to a companion branch-and-cut paper then in preparation (pp. 2, 6, 19).
positioning: Extends the polyhedral approach of Fischetti-Toth (ATSP) and Ascheuer et al. and Balas-Fischetti-Pulleyblank (precedence-constrained ATSP) to time windows, against the big-M standard model and the van Eijl / Maffioli-Sciomachen model (pp. 3, 5, 12).
writing: Theorem-proof paper whose conclusion restates the model's advantage and its one drawback (objectives) and admits that facet proofs look very difficult (pp. 18-19).
limits_future: No makespan or waiting-time objectives; small set-up time changes reshape the polytope, so only validity is proved; the companion branch-and-cut is reported better than earlier LP-based methods on loosely constrained classes (pp. 11, 18-19).

method_links.note: Steps 1-2, joint, 1997: the time variables and their big-M links are dropped, only arc variables remain and time windows become cuts; the model is expected to be 'superior to alternative ones, at least for some problem classes', and the companion result is stated per instance class (loosely constrained).

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: side constraints enter an arc model only as no-good path constraints that are then lifted; capacity constraints could be modelled the same way; reused as PECs in S057 and S125

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Chvátal–Gomory derivation as validity proof and separation handle
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: V-lifting is a 1/2-weighted combination of valid inequalities followed by rounding
every inequality valid for the ATSP polytope or the precedence-constrained ATSP has a version valid for P_TW

transferable: Replace big-M time linking by path no-goods on arc variables; validity needs only a cheap sufficient infeasibility test, so separation can start with the deadline check (pp. 5-6).
Lift a path no-good to the transitive closure of the path (tournament form) using only the degree constraints (p. 12).
When facet proofs are out of reach, prove validity and check facetness computationally on tiny instances (PORTA, n <= 5), and say so (p. 11).
To show that a structural question about a polytope (its dimension) is hard, encode a Hamiltonian path question in a single active time window (pp. 10-11).

quotes.text: This has the advantage of avoiding additional variables as well as the associated (typically very ineffective) linking constraints.
proving that certain classes of inequalities are facet defining for PTW appears a very difficult task; hence we only prove the validity of the constraints we propose.

title: On the separation of maximally violated mod-k cuts
contribution: Shows that maximally violated mod-k Chvátal-Gomory cuts of any integer program can be found in O(mn min{m,n}) time by Gaussian elimination modulo a prime, reduces the STSP and ATSP cases to O(|V|) tight sets (O(|V|^2 |E*|) separation), and proves that extended combs and the extended SD-, C3-, NEW1- and D+/D- inequalities are mod-k cuts, with clique lifting and 2-cycle cloning read through mod-k derivations; the journal version of S139.
problem_entry: Few TSP facet classes have exact polynomial separation and combs have none; Applegate-Bixby-Chvátal-Cook's idea of maximally violated combs and Letchford's observation that zero-weight binary clutter problems are congruence systems are carried from mod 2 to mod k for general ILPs (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Restrict to cuts violated by (k-1)/k: drop rows with positive slack, fix the right-hand-side residue to k-1 and solve the congruence system in GF(k); for the TSP only beads and one domino per necklace are needed; ATSP via symmetrized support (pp. 3-10).
assumptions: Integer A and b with P_I != P; known prime factorization for nonprime k; STSP constraints (6)-(8), ATSP constraints (9)-(12) (pp. 1, 3-4, 6, 9).
proof_devices: Scaling of the multipliers in GF(k) (Theorem 2), p. 4; reduction modulo a prime factor (Theorem 3), p. 5
Replacing a tight SEC by a combination of tight rows equal mod k (Theorem 4), p. 7; induction over dominoes (Theorem 6), pp. 8-9
Clique lifting keeps the mod-k property when the loop-coefficient multipliers lambda_v are nonnegative (Theorem 11), p. 15
A mod-k derivation as an easily checked sufficient condition for the validity of 2-cycle cloning, whose validity check is NP-complete in general (Theorem 12), p. 16

Explicit multipliers showing extended combs, SD, C3, NEW1 and D+/D- families to be mod-2, mod-3 and mod-k cuts (Theorems 10, 13-16), pp. 12, 17-19; computer checks of a mod-2 facet for |V| >= 12 and of NEW1, pp. 13, 18
experiments: none; the practical use of the separation is left open (p. 19).
positioning: Follows Applegate-Bixby-Chvátal-Cook and Fleischer-Tardos, generalizes Caprara-Fischetti {0,1/2}-cuts, credits Letchford's observation, and places itself next to lift-and-project and Gomory cuts as separation of large implicit classes (pp. 2-3, 19).
writing: Theorem sequence with a reframing sentence ('puts comb separation in a different light') and an open question about lifting answered for the ATSP (pp. 11-12).
limits_future: General mod-k separation remains NP-hard even for k = 2; no minimal solution guaranteed for nonprime k; future: undominated mod-k TSP cuts, other problems, practical use (pp. 4-5, 19).

method_links.note: As in S139: the separation sub-decision is written as its own integer program but solved, in its maximally violated case only, by linear algebra in GF(k), not by a general-purpose solver; nothing is implemented, a counter-case to the taste warning against an algorithm without implementation and test.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Restrict separation to maximally violated cuts
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: an NP-hard separation becomes a congruence system once only cuts violated by (k-1)/k are sought

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Chvátal–Gomory derivation as validity proof and separation handle
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: explicit multipliers prove extended combs, SD, C3, NEW1 and D+/D- families to be mod-k cuts, and a derivation certifies 2-cycle cloning

transferable: To show that a lifting operation keeps an inequality inside a cut class, extend its Chvátal-Gomory multipliers to the lifted graph (lambda_v from the loop coefficients, p. 15).
Use a known rank-1 derivation as a cheap sufficient validity test for an operation whose exact validity check is NP-complete (2-cycle cloning, p. 16).
Before solving the congruence system, drop the tight bound constraints (complement upper bounds) and every row with slack >= theta (p. 5).
For cuts that need not be maximally violated, add rows in order of increasing slack until the congruence system becomes solvable (p. 5).

quotes.text: Theorem 5 puts comb separation in a different light, in that it allows for efficient exact separation of maximally violated members of the family of mod-2 cuts which contains, among others, comb inequalities.

Interestingly, at least for the case of extended comb inequalities both operations do not increase the Chvátal rank [29] of the starting inequality, and also preserve the property of being a mod-2 cut.

title: Models and algorithms for optimizing cell suppression in tabular data with linear constraints
contribution: Introduces a Benders-type integer model for secondary cell suppression in tables linked by any system of linear equations, solves it by branch-and-cut with attacker-LP separation and strengthened capacity, cover and bridgeless cuts, and reports the first proven optima for a real 4-D table with marginals and for linked tables plus 1,160 random 3- and 4-D tables (the same results appear in S072).
problem_entry: EU ESPRIT disclosure-control project; earlier methods are heuristic and two-dimensional and Kelly's MILP is huge; the paper takes tables linked by a generic linear system (k-D, hierarchical, linked), 'the first attempt' in this setting (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Project the two attacker tables per sensitive cell out of the classical model by LP duality ('inspired by Benders’ decomposition'), leaving capacity cuts on the suppression variables that are separated by solving the attacker LP and reading its dual (pp. 3-5, 12-13).
assumptions: Table y with My = b and attacker bounds lb <= y <= ub; for k-D tables with marginals M has entries 0 and ±1 and b = 0, a network only for k = 2; lower, upper and sliding protection levels; nonnegative weights; a continuous LP attacker (pp. 2-3, 12).
proof_devices: LP duality projection of the attacker subproblems, finitely many extreme dual solutions giving undominated capacity constraints, pp. 4, 12-13
Polynomial solvability of the LP relaxation by the equivalence of separation and optimization, p. 5
Coefficient capping at the right-hand side for 0-1 variables (strengthened capacity constraints), p. 5
experiments: ANSI C, CPLEX 3.0, Pentium II/266; 10 real tables (2-D, 3-D, 4-D, linked) all solved; 1,160 random 3-/4-D tables, 10 per class, 3-hour limit on a Pentium II/400, solved counts per class; time grows exponentially with table size, root gaps moderate; no other method run as baseline (pp. 7-12).
positioning: Builds on Fischetti-Salazar 1999 (2-D) against Kelly's MILP, Geurts and the heuristics of Kelly-Golden-Assad, Robertson and Sande; written for a statistics audience (pp. 1-2, 6).
writing: Opens with the Willenborg-de Waal worked example of an attacker's range, gives an intuitive reading of capacity constraints, and states firsts ('the first attempt', first optima for 4-D and linked tables) (pp. 1-2, 4, 12).
limits_future: Initial heuristic 'rather poor'; 4-D instance much harder; exponential growth with table size; future: CSP-lib, a public test library with solutions (pp. 7-8, 11-12).

method_links.note: Step 3, joint: the per-cell attacker tables are projected out by LP duality into capacity cuts on the suppression variables, and the move is named Benders (the S069 card noted that the 1999 2-D paper did not use the word).
The classical model is dismissed by a size count ('a size that cannot be handled explicitly'), not by running a solver on it.
Dated lapse, 2000: the authors state as their opinion that their initial heuristic is at least comparable to practitioners' suppression procedures, without running any of them.
Step 6: losses printed: the poor initial heuristic, the hard 4-D case and the exponential growth of running time.

transferable: When a requirement must hold for an adversary's continuous LP (attacker, recourse, follower), dualize that LP and impose the requirement as cuts on the master's binaries; separate by solving the LP at the master point and reading its dual (pp. 3-5, 12-13).
On 0-1 variables, cap every cut coefficient at the right-hand side before adding the cut (p. 5).
Forbid redundant choices with a tiny fictitious requirement on every chosen nonessential item (bridgeless inequalities, p. 5).
Report the root-node upper and lower gaps, so that stopping after the root becomes a heuristic with a certified bound (pp. 8, 11-12).

quotes.text: The capability of benchmarking known heuristics is thus another important feature of our exact solution methodology.
We are convinced that the availability of a common test bed for comparing different solution procedures can be of great help to researchers in the field.

title: A polyhedral approach to simplified crew scheduling and vehicle scheduling problems
contribution: Argues that the weak single-commodity arc model can beat set partitioning on loosely constrained crew and vehicle scheduling instances with few depots, strengthens it with five cut families (PEC, EPEC, CLIQUE, GCUT, LPI) with exact or heuristic separation, and evaluates two branch-and-cut codes on MD-VSP (results shared with S125) and basic CSP instances, with an ablation of three generic speed-ups.
problem_entry: Three classical models compared in words; a threshold hardness of duty rules and depot count below which the arc model can compete, argued from the one-depot, no-rule extreme case (a transportation problem) and from the conjecture that long duties help the arc model and hurt set partitioning (pp. 2-4).
key_idea: Arc model with infeasible-path constraints whose LP relaxation is polynomial given an infeasibility oracle, strengthened by compatibility-flag cuts, and a cut loop that separates points moved towards the incumbents (pp. 7-13, 20).
assumptions: n trips with times and weights, d depots with m_k crews or vehicles, spread- and working-time limits, transition costs (+infinity for forbidden pairs); acyclic trip graph; costs per transition only, no duty-level or depot-dependent costs (pp. 3, 5-6, 22-23).
proof_devices: Polynomial LP relaxation given a membership oracle: only O(n^2) support paths need checking (Savelsbergh), pp. 7-8
EPEC validity by counting the arcs among disjoint paths inside S, p. 10
LPI validity as a rank-1 Chvátal-Gomory combination with multipliers 1/3 and 2/3, p. 13
Exact CLIQUE separation by total unimodularity of a bipartite incidence matrix, p. 16
Transposition: reversing time maps valid inequalities to valid transposed ones, p. 12
experiments: FORTRAN, CPLEX 6.0, APC, Digital Alpha 533 MHz; MD-VSP random instances (10 per class) and 15 bus-company instances, all on the web; BMR, Beasley-Cao and Mingozzi et al. times copied from other machines with caveats; ablation of three devices with a 10,000 s limit and unsolved runs averaged at the limit; OR-Library basic CSP classes A and B (pp. 21-28).
positioning: Positions the arc model against set partitioning with column generation (Ribeiro-Soumis, BMR, Mingozzi et al.) and multi-commodity models (Forbes et al., Löbel); credits Reinelt for the interior-point cutting idea and Löbel for Lagrangean pricing (pp. 2-3, 19-20, 22-23).
writing: Argument-first introduction (extreme case, conjecture), then theorems, separation, implementation, and a conclusion that restates the regime where the method wins and admits a poor basic bound (pp. 3-4, 29).
limits_future: Basic lower bound often poor; not competitive on large or tightly constrained CSP instances (long sequences of large LPs); expected intrinsically inferior with trip objections and depot-dependent costs; future: apply the generic speed-up rules elsewhere (pp. 22-23, 26-27, 29).

method_links.note: Step 2, joint: the model is chosen for the instance regime, not for LP strength (weak arc model below a threshold of rule complexity and depot count, and for long duties); step 5: ablation removing three devices one at a time and all together.

Precursor, practice, joint, 2000: the cut loop separates a point moved from x* towards the two best incumbents before x* (credited to Reinelt), and removing it slows the code. My reading: an in-out separation with the incumbents' midpoint as inner point, a decade before the 2009-2010 in-out work of Common Misreading 4.
Dated lapse: rival times copied from other papers on other machines (PC 80486/33; SGI Iris Indigo and Indy) and partly other instances, caveats printed.
Step 6: the losses on large and tightly constrained CSP instances are printed.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: nested EPEC families generated by shrinking min-cut shores, because the joint action of a cut set matters

transferable: Argue a model choice from an extreme case: with no duty rules and one depot the weak model becomes a polynomial transportation problem, while the strong model still fights degeneracy (pp. 3-4).
In the cut loop, separate a convex combination of x* and the two best incumbents (0.1/0.9, then 0.5/0.5, and x* alone if fewer than 15 cuts are found) (p. 20).
Branch on persistently fractional variables: count consecutive LPs in which each variable is fractional and choose among those within 90% of the maximum count (p. 21).
Ablate by disabling one device at a time plus all at once, and average unsolved runs at the time limit, a lower bound on the worsening (pp. 25-26).
Obtain a second cut family by transposition: reverse time and arcs, separate there, transpose the cuts back (pp. 12, 16).
coauthors: Andrea Lodi, Silvano Martello, Paolo Toth

quotes.text: In practice, the choice of the appropriate model depends on the particular structure of the problem in hand.
for large or tightly-constrained instances our branch-and-cut implementation is instead not competitive with the benchmark Mingozzi et al. method based on a set-partitioning model

title: Crew scheduling for Netherlands railways “destination: customer”
contribution: Reports how the TURNI set-covering system (column generation with Lagrangian pricing, Lagrangian selection, fix-and-release passes) was adapted, mainly by recoding data, to NS Reizigers' new 'Destination: Customer' duty rules and used to estimate depot capacities, with a qualitative evaluation against the planners.
problem_entry: An operator's planning question: new duty rules (train teams, variation per duty, series-to-depot assignment) whose effect on depot capacities had to be estimated a priori; VPT only checks duties and CREWS's greedy A* search cannot check per-depot rules (pp. 1-2, 4-7).
key_idea: Set covering with per-depot side constraints solved by TURNI: dynamic-programming duty generation priced by Lagrangian duals, Lagrangian-driven selection, and passes that fix efficient duties and later release some; rules enforced by recoding trips and trains (pp. 7-12).
assumptions: Duty rules handled in generation (9:30 h maximum, meal break after 5:30 h, 25-minute connections); per-depot rules as side constraints; cost mainly the number of duties; weekly cyclic data split into Tuesday, Saturday and Sunday instances (pp. 3, 8, 13).
experiments: Pentium II 450 MHz; train series of up to about 400 trips in seconds to minutes, combined instances of up to 1,000 and about 2,500 trips within one hour, little gain after the second pass; qualitative evaluation by planners and against manual schedules made in parallel; no tables or solver baseline (pp. 12-14).
positioning: Contrasts OR (TURNI) with the AI search of CREWS; places set covering after its airline use and recent railway use; cites the Caprara-Fischetti-Toth set covering heuristic for the dual information (pp. 6-7, 9).
writing: Industrial case report: rules, systems, modelling tricks and qualitative results, ending with a general lesson against greedy constructive heuristics (pp. 1-15).
limits_future: Rules to be relaxed initially; perfect depot match impossible under strict assignment; robustness 'will have to be proved in practice', simulation planned; future: depot-dependent variation rules and whole-day instances of about 8,000 trips (pp. 7, 10, 14).

method_links.note: The model is the kernel: Lagrangian duals of the set covering relaxation drive generation and selection, and greedy duty-by-duty construction is rejected for this class; but the solver is TURNI's own Lagrangian heuristic, not a general-purpose MIP solver.
The baseline is the planners' practice (manual results obtained in parallel; solutions comparable or better than the best manual ones), but no numbers are given.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: passes that fix efficient duties by a score of Lagrangian cost and efficiency, re-solve the rest, and release some fixed duties in the next pass; the same scheme in S081

transferable: Enforce new organisational rules by recoding data attributes the generator already reads (series indicators, train numbers, First/Last flags) instead of writing new constraints (pp. 10-12).
When an instance is infeasible, let a deadheading generator find the missing moves, then add timetabled optional trips close to them and re-solve (p. 12).
Solve separable pieces first (one train series at a time) to learn their peculiarities, then compose the combined instances (p. 13).
Show the running incumbent together with a Lagrangian lower bound so the user can decide when to stop (p. 9).

quotes.text: already after the first fixings, the solutions are typically comparable or better than the best manual ones

A more or less greedy heuristic that successively builds up the individual duties and that has only limited backtracking facilities is deemed to be incapable of capturing the complexities of scheduling drivers and conductors.

title: Solving the cell suppression problem on tabular data with linear constraints
contribution: The Management Science companion of S073: the same Benders-type cell suppression model and branch-and-cut, with the capacity-constraint derivations in full, lifted covers, a parametric preprocessing, pool-based clean-up, a worked example to optimality, and the same computational results plus cut statistics.
problem_entry: As in S073, plus electronic dissemination of hierarchical and linked tables and Sande's LP-based disclosures from published surveys; the 2-D network structure 'does not extend to the general case' (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: A 'new model based on Benders’ decomposition': capacity constraints for upper, lower and sliding protection derived by LP duality from the attacker subproblems, separated per sensitive cell, strengthened, and embedded in branch-and-cut (pp. 3, 5-11).
assumptions: As S073; all capacity-constraint coefficients nonnegative, so constraints with zero right-hand side are dropped (pp. 3-4, 7).
proof_devices: LP duality projection with only extreme points (and rays) of the dual polyhedron giving nondominated constraints, pp. 5-7
Integrality argument for the coefficient cap min{s_i, s_0}, p. 8
Bridgeless inequalities as near-zero right-hand-side capacity constraints, then strengthened, p. 9
experiments: Same hardware, solver and test beds as S073 (10 real tables, 1,160 random tables, 3-hour limit); adds per-family cut counts, pool recoveries and maximum LP rows (Table 3); no baseline method (pp. 12-19).
positioning: Benders instead of the max-flow/min-cut theorem used for 2-D tables; credits Applegate et al. for strong branching and Kelly et al. and Robertson for the heuristic; the reference list cites the 1999 2-D paper but not the JASA article S073, which does not cite it either (pp. 3, 9-10, 19-20).
writing: Adds a worked example of every cut round to proven optimality (pp. 11-12); the introduction says nine real-world instances, section 6 reports ten (pp. 3, 13).
limits_future: Initial heuristic 'rather poor'; 4-D table much harder; random instances harder for lack of structure; no future directions stated (pp. 13-14, 19).

method_links.note: Step 3, joint: the projection is named Benders and named as the tool that replaces max-flow/min-cut once the 2-D network structure is lost.
As in S073, the classical model is dismissed by a size count, not by a solver run.
Dated lapse: the initial heuristic is called 'at least comparable (and often significantly better)' than practitioners' procedures, as an opinion, with none of them run.

Seed the cut pool during preprocessing with the cuts from the duals of LPs solved anyway (p. 10).

title: Solution of real-world train timetabling problems
contribution: Extends the Caprara-Fischetti-Toth Lagrangian timetabling heuristic for a single corridor to manual signaling, station capacities, prescribed timetables, maintenance, periodic train families and two parallel lines, mostly by forbidding or penalizing inside the heuristic, and prices each extension on FS and Ansaldo corridor instances (OCR text, table values lost).
problem_entry: EU rail reform creates the access-to-infrastructure problem; the TRIS project's TCM module must allocate operators' path requests; the basic TTP of [3] lacks several real-world features (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Per-train time-expanded acyclic graphs with shift and stretch profits, cliques of incompatible arcs relaxed in a Lagrangian way (one longest path per train), a ranked one-by-one heuristic with fixing and unfixing, and real-world rules added as forbidden nodes, arcs or penalties (pp. 5-16).
assumptions: Minutes 1-1440 and a daily repeated timetable; constant speed per segment; headways a_i, d_i; time windows; profit = priority minus nondecreasing shift penalty minus linear stretch penalty; maintenance occupation longer than any travel time; nonnegative stretch on alternative routes (pp. 4-5, 12, 16).
experiments: C code, Digital workstation 533 MHz, 1,000 subgradient iterations; 8 corridor instances from FS and Ansaldo; baseline a priority greedy said to approximate manual practice; gains small when the ideal timetable is nearly feasible, above 20% on MU-VR; each extension priced by profit and scheduled trains; no bound or gap reported (pp. 16-22).
positioning: Applies and extends [3] (S002) within an EU project; relax-and-cut noted as impractical for the arc model; a literature list of earlier timetabling work (pp. 3, 9).
writing: Engineering report organized by real-world feature, each with its implementation and its measured price; the conclusion lists claims for infrastructure managers (pp. 10-23).
limits_future: Greedy-equals-manual asserted, not measured; manual signaling, station capacities and periodicity enter the heuristic only (my reading: the relaxation does not see them); TCM being implemented at FS (pp. 10-11, 13, 18, 23).

method_links.note: The practitioner baseline is a proxy, a greedy said to match manual planning, not the planners' own timetables.
[3]'s switch from arc incompatibilities to node-based capacity variables is chosen for multiplier storage and update speed, a model choice driven by the algorithm rather than by the instance class.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: fix the most profitable paths, restart the subgradient, unfix when the bound certifies no improvement; also S061

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: manual signaling, station capacities and periodicity added as forbidden nodes, arcs or penalties inside the constructive heuristic

transferable: Put each unit's feasibility into its own time-expanded acyclic graph so that the relaxed problem per unit is a longest path and only the coupling constraints are dualized (pp. 6, 8-9).

Add a new operational rule first as forbidden nodes or arcs inside the constructive heuristic, and measure its price on the instances it concerns before building it into the relaxation (pp. 10-12, 18-22).
Make periodicity soft: penalize each train's deviation from a running average path of its family instead of forcing identical shifts (pp. 13-14).
coauthors: Alberto Caprara, Pier Luigi Guida, Michele Monaci, Giuseppe Sacco, Paolo Toth

quotes.text: methods proceed in a similar way, therefore the quality of the solution provided by the FS practitioners is close to the value given in this entry.
Typically, if the ideal timetable on input is almost feasible, the best solution found is not much better than the greedy one

title: A branch-and-cut algorithm for the multiple depot vehicle scheduling problem
contribution: Solves the multiple-depot vehicle scheduling problem by branch-and-cut on the arc model with path elimination and lifted path inequalities, max-flow separation with nested and decomposed cuts, separation of points moved towards the incumbents, transportation-problem pricing and fractionality-persistency branching, tested with an ablation on 135 public instances; the results reappear in S057.
problem_entry: MD-VSP is NP-hard; existing exact methods include the BMR set-partitioning scheme, 'heuristic in nature'; the natural arc model 'typically yields poor lower bounds' and needs new cuts (pp. 2-4).
key_idea: PECs for every trip set and depot subset, separated by one max-flow per depot subset and multiplied per round by decomposition, path enumeration and nesting; LPIs as rank-1 cuts; an 'aggressive' cut loop that separates points between x* and the incumbents (pp. 4-12).
assumptions: n trips, m <= n depots with identical vehicles, start/end and travel times, transition and depot costs; complete graph with +infinity arcs, acyclic without depots; random generator of Carpaneto et al. with 5,000 per depot arc (pp. 1-3, 14-15).
proof_devices: PEC dominance over infeasible path constraints by coefficientwise comparison, complement symmetry halving the family, p. 5
Minimum cut in an acyclic network gives the most violated PEC for a fixed depot subset, p. 6
LPI validity as a rank-1 Chvátal-Gomory combination with multipliers 1/3 and 2/3, pp. 9-10
experiments: FORTRAN 77, CPLEX 6.0, Digital Alpha 533 MHz; 120 random instances (10 per class, m = 2, 3, 5) with per-instance tables; BMR's published times with a stated 50x machine factor and caveats; ablation of three devices plus a basic version (10,000 s limit, unsolved runs averaged at the limit); root bound curves per variant; 15 real-world instances, one unsolved with its bound; all 135 instances public (pp. 3, 14-22, 24-25).
positioning: Against BMR set partitioning, column generation and the three-index model; credits Reinelt for the interior-point cutting idea and notes Löbel's independent Lagrangian pricing (pp. 2, 11-12, 19).
writing: Per-instance tables with on-line and off-line gap closure times; claims each device general and extendable to other problems; an appendix documents the instance format (pp. 15-25).
limits_future: Performance deteriorates with several depots because of the many cuts; BMR comparison not immediate; future: trip objections (pp. 18-19, 23).

method_links.note: Precursor, practice, joint: the loop separates points between x* and the two best incumbents before x* (credited to Reinelt, oral communication 1999); without it the root bound on 2-500-01 takes 1,400 s instead of 800 s and class averages worsen. My reading: an in-out separation with the incumbents' midpoint as inner point; it bears on Common Misreading 4.
Step 5: ablation by subtraction, one device at a time plus all three; step 2: the arc model argued for few depots and long duties.
Dated lapse, mitigated: BMR's times come from a PC 80486/33 on other instances; the paper states the machine factor it assumes and the caveats.

transferable: For cuts indexed by a subset of a small set (depots), enumerate only subsets containing a fixed element (complement symmetry), solve one max-flow per subset, and refit the subset greedily once a cut is found (pp. 5-6).
Split a merged violated cut into the connected components of its support; the pieces made the cut loop converge faster (p. 7).
Pause a node whose bound exceeds the best active bound by more than a fixed margin and requeue it (p. 11).
When comparing with published times from another machine, state the speed factor you assume and every difference in instances and counts (p. 19).
Release the instances with a documented file format in an appendix (pp. 24-25).
